_about: Monster families (MONSTER_FAMILIES_DESIGN.md, docs/systems/monster_families_v2_design.md). Each monster's `family` is in monsters.json; this file holds every number the system uses. Tier N needs the Nth number in `thresholds` of DIFFERENT kinds studied; a keystone (a boss, a mini-boss, a seal demon, a monster with proper_noun, or one in the family's `keystones`) counts `keystone_weight` kinds. Abilities are data: `effect` is a primitive in src/family_edges.py and `params` its numbers; `also` adds more parts to one technique. Nothing here scales by floor. `field_note`: one fact-checked piece of folklore per tier (sources: docs/systems/monster_family_field_notes_sources.md); an empty note is hidden.
tier_messages: You know {kin} now. You will recognise every one of them on sight.
You know the signs of {kin} now. You will sense them when you reach a floor.
popup_leads: You have learned how ordinary people kept {kin} away.
You have learned how a hunter takes {kin}.
tier_chronicle: I took enough of {kin} apart that I knew the rest of them on sight.
I learned the signs {kin} leave on a stair, and after that I smelled them coming.
I learned how ordinary people kept {kin} away, the old folk ways, and they worked.
I learned how a hunter takes {kin}, and I started hunting them.
I took apart so many of {kin} that I learned where every one of them breaks.

restless_dead.name: The Restless Dead
restless_dead.blurb: Bodies that would not stay in the ground: bone and dried flesh moved by a will that is not their own. They feel no pain and give no ground, and the grave's sicknesses walk in with them.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The walking dead are ancient. In the Epic of Gilgamesh, the goddess Ishtar threatens to smash the gates of the underworld and bring up the dead to devour the living.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Eyrbyggja saga says that after Thorolf Lame-Foot died, any bird that landed on his grave fell down dead, and the sheep in the valley died. His neighbours knew he walked.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The smell of the grave hangs on the stair: the restless dead walk this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Scottish mourners once laid a wooden platter of salt and earth on a corpse's breast. The antiquary John Brand recorded that the salt stood for the undying spirit, and kept the Devil away.

abilities.name: Grave-Salt
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their paralysis, disease and life drain, and their disease lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Grave-Salt: the salt in your pocket keeps the grave's grip off you.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Grettis saga tells how Grettir the Strong wrestled the draugr Glámr and cut off his head. Then he and the farmer burned the body to cold coals and buried the ashes far from any path.

abilities.name: Bonebreaker
abilities.text: Your blows hit 6% harder when they strike what the dead fear: the weaknesses on their page.
abilities.trigger_msg: Bonebreaker! You strike where the dead are weakest.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: In Eyrbyggja saga, the drowned men of Fróðá came dripping to sit by the fire each night, until Kjartan held a court at the door and charged the dead with trespass. Then they left.

abilities.name: Turn the Dead
abilities.text: A blow at chain 12 or more sends every lesser restless dead in sight fleeing for 6 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: Turn the Dead! The dead in sight shrink back from you.

ghosts.name: Ghosts and Shades
ghosts.blurb: What is left when the body is gone and something refuses to leave. Steel passes through most of them, and their touch takes warmth and courage before it takes life.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: One of the oldest ghost stories is Pliny the Younger's: a chained phantom haunted an Athens house until the philosopher Athenodorus dug where it vanished, found bones in chains, and gave them a proper burial.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Welsh lore told of the corpse candle, a light gliding between the churchyard and a dying person's home. In Shakespeare's England, folk said a blue candle flame meant a spirit was near.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The candle-flames lean the wrong way: ghosts drift on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: In Japan, mourners get a little bag of salt to purify themselves before going home from a funeral. Folk belief in Europe said an iron fence round a graveyard held the dead in place.

abilities.name: Iron and Salt
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their fear and life drain, and their draining no longer heals them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Iron and Salt: the cold iron at your belt breaks the ghost's hold.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Gaels call second sight an dà shealladh, the two sights. Martin Martin wrote in 1703 that a seer who saw a shroud around someone knew death was coming, and the higher it rose, the sooner.

abilities.name: Second Sight
abilities.text: Invisible ghosts within 3 tiles show to you as a faint shimmer you can strike.
abilities.trigger_msg: Second Sight: you see a ghost that the living cannot.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Cornish legend says the ghost of Jan Tregeagle, a harsh steward, was laid by setting him to empty Dozmary Pool with a limpet shell, a task to keep him busy until Judgment Day.

abilities.name: Lay the Ghost
abilities.text: At chain 8 or more, your blows ignore their resistances, as if your weapon were blessed.
abilities.trigger_msg: Lay the Ghost! Your blow bites as if it were blessed.

vampires_liches.name: Vampires and Liches
vampires_liches.blurb: The dead who kept their minds and their hunger. Each one cheated the grave on purpose, by blood or by sorcery, and each one keeps its death hidden somewhere.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Europe's vampire craze grew from Austrian army reports. In 1732 surgeon Johann Flückinger recorded how Serbian villagers staked the dead soldier Arnold Paole, swearing the corpse groaned and bled.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: To find a vampire's grave, villagers led a black stallion through the graveyard, a white one in Albania, and watched where it balked. Holes in the grave's earth were another sign.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The stair smells of iron and old roses: a vampire or a lich keeps court here.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: On St. Andrew's Eve, when Romanians believed the strigoi were most active, families smeared garlic on doors and windows, and young people sat up all night guarding heads of garlic.

abilities.name: Garlic and Ash
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their life drain and paralysis, and their bite no longer heals them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Garlic and Ash: the bite takes nothing back to heal it.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Eastern European folk scattered poppy seed, millet or sand on a suspected vampire's grave, believing it had to count every grain and would spend the whole night at it.

abilities.name: Hunter's Patience
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Hunter's Patience: you take your time with this one.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Vampire hunters chose the stake's wood with care: ash in Russia and the Baltic, hawthorn in Serbia. In 2012 archaeologists at Sozopol, Bulgaria, found two medieval skeletons pinned through the chest with iron rods.

abilities.name: Stake Through the Heart
abilities.text: At chain 18 or more, a lesser vampire or lich below 15% health dies outright: no mist, no rising. A named foe takes a blow 25% harder instead.
abilities.trigger_msg: Stake Through the Heart! It crumbles to ash.

demons.name: Demons and Devils
demons.blurb: Creatures of the Pit, from the smallest tormentor to the princes of Hell. They burn, they lie and they cloud the mind, and every people that met them wrote down a way to send them back.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The word demon comes from the Greek daimon, a spirit that could help or harm. Socrates said a daimonion, an inner voice, held him back whenever he was about to go wrong.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: On a February night in 1855, hoof-like prints appeared in fresh snow across Devon, even on rooftops and high walls, running for many miles. Some people said Satan himself had walked there.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Brimstone on the stair: something from the Pit has climbed this far.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: The Lesser Key of Solomon, a 17th-century grimoire, has the conjurer stand in a nine-foot circle written with holy names, and makes the spirit he calls appear in a triangle outside it.

abilities.name: Circle of Salt
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their burning and confusion, and their burning lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Circle of Salt: the old ring holds against the Pit.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: In the Gospel of Mark, Jesus asks a possessing spirit its name. It answers 'Legion, for we are many,' and he sends the spirits into a herd of pigs that rush into the sea.

abilities.name: True Names
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder.
abilities.trigger_msg: True Names: you call it by its name, and it flinches.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: In the Book of Revelation, an angel comes down with the key to the bottomless pit and a great chain. He binds Satan, the dragon, casts him in and seals it for a thousand years.

abilities.name: Banishment
abilities.text: At chain 18 or more, a lesser demon below 15% health is cast back into the Pit. A named foe takes a blow 25% harder instead.
abilities.trigger_msg: Banishment! It is cast back into the Pit.

dragons.name: Dragons and Wyrms
dragons.blurb: Great scaled serpents with wings or without, old beyond counting and greedy beyond reason. Their breath is weather and their scales are armour, and every one of them has a weak spot somewhere.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: People in Klagenfurt, Austria, took a huge skull dug from a quarry in 1335 for a dragon's. It came from a woolly rhinoceros, and became the model for their dragon statue's head.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: In Beowulf, the dragon's rage begins with a theft: a runaway slave steals a golden cup from its hoard. That night the wyrm wakes and burns the Geats' halls, Beowulf's own among them.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Gold-smell and scorch-marks on the stair: a wyrm lairs on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Knowing that a shield of linden wood would burn, old King Beowulf had one forged all of iron before he went out to fight the dragon.

abilities.name: Dragon-Ward
abilities.text: Their fire, cold and poison hurt you 5% less, and you get +1 on saving throws against their burning, freezing and poison.
abilities.trigger_msg: Dragon-Ward: you turn your shoulder to the breath, the way the old songs say.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: In the Völsunga saga, Sigurd hides in a pit and drives his sword under Fafnir's left shoulder to the hilt. A bearded stranger, Odin in disguise, told him to dig more pits for the blood.

abilities.name: The Soft Belly
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder: Sigurd struck Fafnir from below.
abilities.trigger_msg: The Soft Belly! You strike under the scales.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: In Tolkien's The Hobbit, Bilbo spots a bare patch in the hollow of Smaug's left breast. A thrush carries the news to Bard, whose last arrow strikes home.

abilities.name: The Missing Scale
abilities.text: At chain 12 or more, your blow ignores a dragon's scales and resistances, even Fafnir's.
abilities.trigger_msg: The Missing Scale! Your blow finds the one bare spot.

giants.name: Giants and Trolls
giants.blurb: The old enemies of gods and men: huge, strong and hard to kill. Their danger is their size, and the stories agree that the bigger they are, the harder they fall.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Greeks believed only the one-eyed Cyclopes could have built the walls of Mycenae and Tiryns, where Pausanias said two mules could not shift the smallest stone. Archaeologists still call such walls Cyclopean.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Danish farmers said huge lone boulders were thrown by giants and trolls who hated church bells. A giantess on Langeland hurled Denmark's biggest, Damestenen, at Svindinge church, and it fell short.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The stair shakes underfoot: giants walk this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: In the Book of Samuel, the shepherd boy David turns down King Saul's armour, picks five smooth stones from a brook, and drops the giant Goliath with a single stone from his sling.

abilities.name: Steady Hand
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steady Hand: its size does not rush you.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Norwegian legend says a troll wedding party celebrated all night in Romsdal until sunrise caught them and turned them all to stone. Peaks of Trolltindene are still called the Bride and the Groom.

abilities.name: Fire and Dawn
abilities.text: Your blows stop their regeneration for 3 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: Fire and Dawn: the wound will not close.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: An English tale set in Cornwall says Jack dug a deep pit, lured the giant Cormoran into it with a blast on his horn, and killed him, earning the name Jack the Giant Killer.

abilities.name: The Bigger They Are
abilities.text: At chain 5 or more, your weapon hits them 5% harder, and 8% harder against a giant that fills more than one tile.
abilities.trigger_msg: The Bigger They Are! It staggers under the blow.

goblinkin.name: Goblins and Orcs
goblinkin.blurb: The warband peoples of the tunnels, who live by raiding and by numbers. They are brave in a crowd and cowardly alone, and they lay traps for anyone who walks without looking.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Tolkien took the word orc from Old English. Beowulf lists orcneas, perhaps meaning 'demon-corpses', among the monsters descended from Cain, beside giants and elves.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Cornish tin miners heard knockers, small spirits of the mine, tapping in the rock. Some said the knocking led to rich ore, others that it warned of a cave-in.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Crude marks scratched on the stair: a goblin warband holds this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: In George MacDonald's The Princess and the Goblin, the miner's boy Curdie drives goblins back by singing rhymes, which they hate, and stamping on their soft feet, a goblin's one weak spot.

abilities.name: Break Their Nerve
abilities.text: When you kill one, each lesser goblin or orc in sight may lose its nerve and flee for 4 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: Break Their Nerve! The warband wavers.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: In Christina Rossetti's poem Goblin Market, Lizzie stands firm while the goblin men squash their enchanted fruit against her face. She never opens her mouth, and carries the juice home to save her sister Laura.

abilities.name: Trap-Wise
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their fear and bleeding, and their ambushers never catch you unawares.
abilities.trigger_msg: Trap-Wise: you saw that coming.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: In Tolkien's The Hobbit, the Great Goblin howls with rage at Orcrist, which goblins call Biter. When Gandalf's Glamdring, which they call Beater, cuts him down, his soldiers flee shrieking.

abilities.name: Your Name Is Known
abilities.text: Lesser goblins and orcs flee from you on sight.
abilities.trigger_msg: Your Name Is Known: the warband scatters at the sight of you.

mortals.name: Mortal Foes
mortals.blurb: Men and women who came down here by choice, to rob, to worship or to kill for pay. They bleed like you and think like you, which makes them the least predictable thing in the dark.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The word assassin comes from the Nizari Ismailis of Alamut castle in Persia, whom their enemies called hashishin. Marco Polo spread tales of their leader, the Old Man of the Mountain.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: In Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves, a robber chalks Ali Baba's door so the gang can find it at night. The clever slave girl Morgiana chalks the same mark on the neighbours' doors.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Bootprints and a cold campfire on the stair: armed men and women walk this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Greek myth's master thief Autolycus could change the look of the cattle he stole. So Sisyphus set lead letters in his cattle's hooves, and the hoofprints accused Autolycus by name.

abilities.name: Read Their Hands
abilities.text: The thieves among them can never steal from you.
abilities.trigger_msg: Read Their Hands: you catch the hand before it reaches your purse.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Swiss legend says the bailiff Gessler made William Tell shoot an apple off his son's head. Tell struck it with one arrow, then admitted the second arrow in his quiver had been meant for Gessler.

abilities.name: Steady Hand
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steady Hand: you have fought his kind before.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: In Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur, Lancelot beats three knights who had set upon Sir Kay, and spares them on one condition: each must go to King Arthur's court and yield himself to Queen Guinevere.

abilities.name: Yield!
abilities.text: At chain 8 or more, a lesser foe below half health surrenders, throws down his purse and runs.
abilities.trigger_msg: Yield! Your foe throws down his purse and runs.

fair_folk.name: The Fair Folk
fair_folk.blurb: The hidden people of the mounds and the deep woods, beautiful and dangerous and never quite honest. They bargain and bewitch, and they keep every promise exactly as it was worded.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Irish and Scots called them the Good Neighbours or the Fair Folk rather than fairies, because speaking of them plainly might draw their attention, and their anger.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: A ring of mushrooms marked where the Fair Folk danced, people said. A Welsh tale says Rhys danced in one for months, yet swore when his friend pulled him out that it was five minutes.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: A ring of mushrooms on the stair: the Fair Folk are abroad on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: In Devon and Cornwall, a traveller who was pixy-led, wandering lost in a field he knew well, turned his coat inside out to break the spell and find his way home.

abilities.name: Coat Turned Inside Out
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their confusion, sleep and charm.
abilities.trigger_msg: Coat Turned Inside Out: their glamour slides off you.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: In a Highland tale, a smith rescues his son from inside a fairy hill by driving his dirk into the threshold. The cold iron keeps the hill from closing behind him.

abilities.name: Cold Iron
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder, and 10% harder if it is iron or cold iron.
abilities.trigger_msg: Cold Iron! The Fair Folk cannot abide it.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: In the Grimms' tale, the queen keeps her child by guessing the little man's name, Rumpelstiltskin. In a rage he stamps his foot deep into the ground, then tears himself in two.

abilities.name: Their True Name
abilities.text: Invisible or disguised Fair Folk within 4 tiles show to you, and their charm can never take you.
abilities.trigger_msg: Their True Name: you name it, and its glamour falls away.

great_beasts.name: Great Beasts
great_beasts.blurb: Animals grown huge and savage, and the legendary quarry of the old hunting tales. They have no magic but muscle, tooth and claw, and that is usually enough.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Northern peoples feared the bear so much they avoided its name. English 'bear' probably began as 'the brown one', and the Slavic medved means 'honey-eater'.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Old English poets had a sure sign that blood would soon be spilled: the wolf, the raven and the eagle gathering before the fighting, the beasts of battle waiting for the feast.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Fresh tracks and torn bark on the stair: great beasts hunt this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Norse myth says the cook Andhrímnir boils the boar Sæhrímnir every day to feed Odin's warriors in Valhalla, and every evening the boar is whole again.

abilities.name: Hunter's Harvest
abilities.text: Harvesting their corpses gives one extra portion.
abilities.trigger_msg: Hunter's Harvest: you know where the best cuts are.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Heracles chased the Erymanthian Boar into deep snow until it floundered, then caught it and carried it alive to King Eurystheus, who was so frightened he hid in a bronze jar.

abilities.name: Steady Hand
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steady Hand: you read the beast before it moves.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Aulus Gellius tells of Androcles, a runaway slave who pulled a huge splinter from a lion's paw. Thrown to the beasts in Rome's Great Circus, he met the same lion, and it fawned on him.

abilities.name: Beast-Friend
abilities.text: One lesser beast in ten arrives calm and leaves you be unless you strike first.
abilities.trigger_msg: Beast-Friend: the beasts here watch you and let you pass.

vermin.name: Vermin, Spiders and Swarms
vermin.blurb: The small biters of the dark: things that crawl, gnaw, spin and sting, often by the hundred. Alone they are a nuisance; together they carry poison and plague, and the patient ones wait in silk.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Ovid tells of Arachne, a weaver whose flawless tapestry of the gods' misdeeds enraged Athena, who turned her into a spider. Her name is the Greek word for spider, and spiders are still arachnids.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: A rat king is a knot of rats tangled by their tails, and folk took one as an omen of plague. A museum in Altenburg, Germany, keeps a mummified knot of 32 rats.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Webs and gnawed bones on the stair: vermin and spiders creep on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: In Apulia, people believed a tarantula's bite had to be danced out in frenzied tarantellas, sometimes for days. Legend says four thieves of Toulouse robbed plague victims unharmed, protected by vinegar steeped in herbs.

abilities.name: Web and Plague
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their poison, disease, slowing and holding, and their poison and disease last a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Web and Plague: you clean the bite and step through the silk.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: At Jōren Falls in Japan, legend says a man resting by the water felt silk threads winding round his leg. He slipped them onto a tree stump, which the jorōgumo spider dragged into the falls.

abilities.name: Tremor-Sense
abilities.text: Vermin and spiders waiting in ambush within 4 tiles are revealed to you.
abilities.trigger_msg: Tremor-Sense: a thread trembles, and you see what waits on it.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: In 1284, legend says, a piper in coloured clothes led Hamelin's rats into the River Weser with his tune. Cheated of his fee, he came back and led away 130 children.

abilities.name: The Piper's Tune
abilities.text: A blow at chain 8 or more sends every lesser vermin and spider in sight fleeing for 5 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: The Piper's Tune! The swarm turns tail.

serpents.name: Serpents and Swamp-Kin
serpents.blurb: Snakes great and small, and the scaled and slimy folk of the flooded halls. They strike fast, their venom works slowly, and they coil where you least expect them.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Buddhist tradition says that when a great storm broke over the meditating Buddha, the naga king Mucalinda wrapped him in seven coils and spread his hood over his head for seven days.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: In the Epic of Gilgamesh, a snake steals the plant of rejuvenation while Gilgamesh bathes in a pool, and sheds its skin as it slips away. Ever since, the story suggests, snakes have renewed themselves.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: A shed skin on the stair: serpents coil on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: When Cleopatra died, said to be by an asp's bite, Octavian sent for the Psylli, a Libyan people believed immune to snakebite, to draw out the venom. It was too late.

abilities.name: Antivenom
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their poison and paralysis, and their poison lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Antivenom: you know which herb to chew.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Pliny the Elder wrote that the ichneumon, the Egyptian mongoose, rolled in mud again and again, baking each coat hard in the sun as armour before it fought the asp.

abilities.name: Mongoose
abilities.text: Your first blow in a fight against one starts at chain 2.
abilities.trigger_msg: Mongoose! You strike before it can.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Pliny wrote that the Marsi of central Italy, said to descend from Circe's son, could send snakes to sleep. Every May 1 in Cocullo, their old land, snake-catchers drape Saint Dominic's statue with live snakes.

abilities.name: Snake-Charmer
abilities.text: At chain 8 or more, a lesser serpent you strike is charmed calm for 8 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: Snake-Charmer: it sways, and settles.

birds.name: Birds and Winged Hunters
birds.blurb: Hunters of the air, some of them birds and some only partly. They dive at the eyes and are gone again before you can swing.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: In Ferdowsi's Shahnameh, the great bird Simurgh raised the abandoned baby Zal in her nest. When he left, she gave him one of her feathers: burn it, and she would come.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Rome's founding turned on birds: Remus saw six vultures, then Romulus saw twelve, and each brother claimed the gods had chosen him.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Feathers drift down the stair: winged hunters nest on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Emperor Frederick II wrote in the 1240s that Arab falconers were the first to hood their hawks, and he adopted the hood for its great usefulness. A hooded bird sits calm in the dark.

abilities.name: Hooded
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their blinding and confusion, as a falconer's hood calms a hawk.
abilities.trigger_msg: Hooded: you keep your eyes covered and your head clear.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: In the Mahabharata, Drona sets a target bird in a tree and asks his pupils what they see. Arjuna alone answers that he sees only its head, and his arrow strikes the head off.

abilities.name: Falconer's Eye
abilities.text: Your bow and your thrown weapons hit them 5% harder.
abilities.trigger_msg: Falconer's Eye! You lead the target just right.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: For his sixth labour, Heracles could not reach the Stymphalian Birds in their marsh, so Athena gave him bronze krotala, rattles made by Hephaestus. Their clatter scared the birds aloft, where he shot them.

abilities.name: Heracles' Rattle
abilities.text: At chain 12 or more, the din of your blow sends every lesser winged hunter in sight scattering for 6 turns.
abilities.trigger_msg: Heracles' Rattle! The flock scatters.

gorgons.name: Gorgons and Basilisks
gorgons.blurb: Creatures whose look alone can stop a heart or turn flesh to stone. The ancients survived them by never meeting their eyes.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Greeks painted a Gorgon's glaring face, the gorgoneion, on shields, temple roofs and the bottoms of cups, believing it scared off evil. Athena wore Medusa's head on her aegis.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Pliny wrote that the basilisk's hiss sent every other snake fleeing, and that it scorched the grass and burst the stones wherever it passed.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Stone figures stand on the stair, their faces frozen in fear: a gorgon's gaze haunts this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Medieval lore said never to meet a basilisk's eyes. Pliny named the weasel as its killer, and in Cantabria, Spain, travellers into basilisk country carried a rooster, whose crow was believed fatal to it.

abilities.name: Averted Eyes
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their killing gaze and their poison.
abilities.trigger_msg: Averted Eyes: you look at its feet, never its face.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Perseus never looked at Medusa. Apollodorus says he watched her in a polished bronze shield while Athena guided his hand, and cut off her head as she slept.

abilities.name: Perseus' Shield
abilities.text: While you carry a shield, their gaze cannot take you at all.
abilities.trigger_msg: Perseus' Shield: you watch it in the bright metal, and the gaze slides off.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Hermes gave Perseus the harpe, a sickle-sword of adamant, for Medusa's neck. Medieval lore added that a basilisk forced to see itself in a mirror would be slain by its own stare.

abilities.name: Harpe
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder, and at chain 18 or more a lesser one below half health meets its own stare and turns to stone. A named foe takes a blow 25% harder instead.
abilities.trigger_msg: Harpe! It meets its own stare and turns to stone.

legend.name: Monsters of Legend
legend.blurb: The beasts that heroes became famous for killing, each one the answer to an old story. Most of them were beaten once, by someone who knew the trick.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: In Lycia, in today's Turkey, natural gas flames have burned from the rocks of Yanartaş for at least 2,500 years. The site is also called the Chimaera, after the fire-breathing monster.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Plutarch says Athens sent seven youths and seven maidens to the Minotaur every nine years, on a ship with a black sail, because everyone believed they were sailing to their deaths.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The stair is carved with an old story: a monster of legend waits on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Circe told Odysseus to row past Scylla's cliff at top speed, not fight: better to lose six men than his whole ship to Charybdis. He held his course, and lost six.

abilities.name: Steady Hand
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steady Hand: you know how this story goes.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Each time Heracles cut off one of the Hydra's heads, two grew back. His nephew Iolaus seared each stump with a burning brand, and the heads stopped returning.

abilities.name: Iolaus' Torch
abilities.text: Your blows stop their regeneration for 3 turns, so a hydra's heads stay down.
abilities.trigger_msg: Iolaus' Torch: you sear the wound, and it stays shut.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Ariadne gave Theseus a ball of thread to unwind as he walked into the Labyrinth. After killing the Minotaur, he followed it back out of the maze Daedalus built to hold the beast.

abilities.name: Know the Story
abilities.text: Once per fight, your first wrong answer against one does not end your chain. You know how the story ends.
abilities.trigger_msg: Know the Story: you remember how it ends, and keep going.

shapeshifters.name: Werebeasts and Shapeshifters
shapeshifters.blurb: People who are not always people, and animals who are not always animals. They hide in plain sight until the moon, the hunger or the moment turns them.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Herodotus heard that every one of the Neuri, a people beyond the Scythians, turned into a wolf for a few days once a year. He added that the tale did not convince him.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: In Petronius's Satyricon, a wolf raiding a farm's flock is speared in the neck. Next day the soldier who turned into a wolf the night before lies in bed while a doctor tends his neck.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Claw-marks and a torn cloak on the stair: a shapeshifter hunts this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Hunters poisoned wolves with wolfsbane, or aconite. Greek myth said it grew from Cerberus's drool when Heracles dragged him from the underworld, and medieval doctors even tried it as a cure for werewolves.

abilities.name: Wolfsbane
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their bleeding and disease, and their bleeding lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Wolfsbane: the wound closes clean.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Legend says Jean Chastel killed the Beast of Gévaudan in 1767 with a silver bullet. Historians trace the silver to novelists from 1935, though 19th-century German folklore already made silver a werewolf's bane.

abilities.name: Silvered
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 3% harder, and 10% harder if it is silver.
abilities.trigger_msg: Silvered! The shape it wears cannot stand it.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: In the Odyssey, Menelaus holds the sea god Proteus fast while he becomes a lion, a serpent, a leopard, a boar, running water and a tree. Worn out, Proteus answers his questions.

abilities.name: Forced Shape
abilities.text: At chain 8 or more, a lesser shapeshifter is stunned for 3 turns as its shape tears.
abilities.trigger_msg: Forced Shape! Its shape tears, and it reels.

constructs.name: Golems and Constructs
constructs.blurb: Things made, not born: stone, clay, bronze and clockwork given motion by craft or magic. They feel no pain and no fear, and they obey their last order forever.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Homer's Iliad tells of golden handmaidens made by the smith god Hephaestus. They looked like living girls, had minds, voices and strength, and helped their lame master walk.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: In the old English tale of Friar Bacon, his brass head finally spoke while his servant Miles kept watch: 'Time is.' 'Time was.' 'Time is past.' Miles never woke Bacon, and the head broke apart.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Grinding stone and ticking brass on the stair: something made, not born, guards this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: In the Prague legend, Rabbi Loew pulled the shem, God's name on a slip, from his golem's mouth every Friday so it rested on the Sabbath. Once he forgot, and it ran wild.

abilities.name: Steady Hand
abilities.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock when you attack them.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steady Hand: it is slow, and so you need not be quick.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Apollodorus says Medea promised the bronze giant Talos immortality, then drew out the bronze nail that sealed his one vein at the ankle. All his ichor gushed out, and he died.

abilities.name: Find the Seam
abilities.text: At chain 8 or more, your blows ignore their resistances, as Medea pulled the nail from Talos's ankle.
abilities.trigger_msg: Find the Seam! Your blow goes in where the plates join.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Golem tales from Poland, and later Prague, put emet, 'truth', on the brow: rub out the first letter, leaving met, 'dead', and it falls. Elijah of Chełm's golem scarred his face as he unmade it.

abilities.name: Erase the Letter
abilities.text: At chain 18 or more, a lesser construct below 15% health falls lifeless: emet, truth, becomes met, dead. A named foe takes a blow 25% harder instead.
abilities.trigger_msg: Erase the Letter! Truth becomes dead, and it falls.

elementals.name: Elementals and Djinn
elementals.blurb: Living fire, stone, wind and water, and the spirits of smokeless flame. They are the world's raw stuff with a temper.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: The Greek thinker Empedocles taught that all things are made of four roots: earth, water, air and fire. Legend says he leapt into Mount Etna, which threw back one of his bronze sandals.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Sailors called the blue flames that danced on their mastheads in storms St. Elmo's fire. Ancient Greek sailors saw the twins Castor and Pollux in a pair of such lights, a sign of safe passage.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The air on the stair tastes of lightning and ash: elementals stir on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Pliny claimed the salamander was so cold it put out fire on contact. Fireproof asbestos was later taken for salamander's hair, and the legendary Prester John was said to own a robe of it.

abilities.name: Ward of the Elements
abilities.text: Their fire, cold, lightning and acid hurt you 5% less.
abilities.trigger_msg: Ward of the Elements: you meet the element and it gives a little.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Aristotle taught that each element had two qualities: fire hot and dry, water cold and wet, air hot and wet, earth cold and dry. Fire and water share none at all.

abilities.name: Opposing Element
abilities.text: Your blows hit 6% harder when they strike what the elemental is weak to.
abilities.trigger_msg: Opposing Element! Water on fire.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: In The Fisherman and the Jinni, a fisherman nets a copper jar sealed with Solomon's seal. Out pours a furious jinni, and the fisherman tricks it back inside by asking how it could ever fit.

abilities.name: Solomon's Seal
abilities.text: Their burning and freezing wear off twice as fast, and their elemental damage hurts you 10% less.
abilities.trigger_msg: Solomon's Seal: the seal holds the element in check.

oozes.name: Oozes and Slimes
oozes.blurb: Mindless, shapeless eaters that clean the dungeon of everything soft. They dissolve what they touch, and cutting the wrong one only makes more of it.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Since at least the 1300s, people in Britain have found blobs of jelly on the grass and blamed shooting stars. Welsh shepherds called it pwdre ser, 'rot of the stars'.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: Japanese lore tells of the nuppeppō, a wandering lump of flab with a face in its folds, that reeks of rotting flesh and shuffles through deserted streets at night.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The stair is slick and smells of acid: oozes creep on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Germanic and Scandinavian folk believed a yellow jelly on the gate, witches' butter, meant a witch had cursed the house. Stabbing it with metal pins was said to break the spell.

abilities.name: Clean Blade
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their paralysis and weakness, and their weakness lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Clean Blade: you wipe the slime off before it takes hold.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: In the Devi Mahatmya, every drop of the demon Raktabija's blood that touched the ground sprang up as another Raktabija. So the goddess Kali drank the blood as it flowed, before a drop could fall.

abilities.name: Strike True
abilities.text: Your blows never split them, and your weapon hits them 5% harder.
abilities.trigger_msg: Strike True! A clean blow, and it does not split.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: In the 1958 film The Blob, Steve, played by Steve McQueen, realises the creature cannot stand cold. The town freezes it with fire extinguishers, and the Air Force flies it to the Arctic.

abilities.name: Fire and Frost
abilities.text: Your blows hit 10% harder when they strike what an ooze is weak to.
abilities.trigger_msg: Fire and Frost! It shrivels from the blow.

aberrations.name: Aberrations
aberrations.blurb: Things that should not exist: minds from beyond the stars, eyes that float, mouths that wait. They attack the mind as much as the body, and many of them are not what they seem.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: In 1752 Bishop Erik Pontoppidan wrote that the Norwegian kraken was so vast its back was mistaken for islands. The giant squid, first photographed alive in 2004, may lie behind the tale.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: In H. P. Lovecraft's The Call of Cthulhu, sailors on the risen city of R'lyeh find its angles wrong. One man is swallowed by an angle that is acute but behaves as if obtuse.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: The stair feels wrong, as if it bends: aberrations lurk on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: In the Odyssey, Odysseus plugs his crew's ears with beeswax and has them tie him to the mast to hear the Sirens. When he begs to be freed, they bind him tighter.

abilities.name: Steel Mind
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their confusion and paralysis, and their hallucinations last a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Steel Mind: you hold onto what is real.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Japanese lore says a tool that reaches its hundredth year can come alive as a tsukumogami. A medieval scroll tells of old tools thrown out before that birthday, which came alive anyway, full of spite.

abilities.name: Mimic-Sense
abilities.text: A disguised mimic within 2 tiles gives itself away to you.
abilities.trigger_msg: Mimic-Sense: something about that one is wrong.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: The giant Argus had a hundred eyes and never closed them all at once, so nothing slipped past him. After Hermes charmed him asleep and slew him, Hera set his eyes in the peacock's tail.

abilities.name: The Unblinking
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder, and their ambushers never catch you unawares.
abilities.trigger_msg: The Unblinking! You never looked away.

plants.name: Plants and Fungi
plants.blurb: Green and grey things that grow where nothing should: mould, vine and walking rot. They cannot chase you far, so they make you come to them, or put you to sleep where you stand.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: In 1874 the New York World printed a German botanist's account of a man-eating tree in Madagascar. Reporter Edmund Spencer had made it all up, yet explorers went hunting for the tree for decades.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: In Shakespeare's Macbeth, a vision the witches raise promises Macbeth he is safe until Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane. Then a messenger sees the forest moving: soldiers carrying cut boughs.

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: Spores drift on the stair like dust: something green and hungry grows on this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Plague doctors of the 1600s wore beaked masks stuffed with lavender, peppermint, cloves and myrrh, believing the sweet scents would ward off the bad air thought to carry disease.

abilities.name: Herbalist's Mask
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their poison, sleep and hallucinations, and their poison lasts a tenth less time.
abilities.trigger_msg: Herbalist's Mask: you breathe through the cloth.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: Medieval lore said a pulled mandrake shrieked and killed all who heard it. So gatherers tied it to a dog, which dragged it free, a trick Josephus described in the first century.

abilities.name: Herbalist
abilities.text: Harvesting them gives one extra portion.
abilities.trigger_msg: Herbalist: you know which parts are worth keeping.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Around 723, Boniface took an axe to Donar's Oak, a tree sacred to Thor at Geismar. His biographer says a blast from above helped topple it, and Boniface built a chapel from its timber.

abilities.name: Woodsman's Axe
abilities.text: Your weapon hits them 5% harder, and their ambushers never catch you unawares.
abilities.trigger_msg: Woodsman's Axe! You cut low, where it grows from.

celestials.name: Celestials
celestials.blurb: Creatures of heaven and of the gods' service, some still pure and some gone wrong. Their light blinds, their purpose is fixed, and they rarely start a fight.

tiers.name: Recognise
tiers.field_note: Europeans once believed unicorn horn could detect poison, and kings treasured it. Most such horns were narwhal tusks, and Denmark's coronation throne, built in the 1660s, is made of them.

abilities.name: Recognise
abilities.text: Every member of the family you see has its full Bestiary page, and looking at one names its family.

tiers.name: Forewarned
tiers.field_note: In the Gospel of Luke, shepherds watching their flock by night are terrified when an angel appears and the glory of the Lord shines round them. The angel's first words are 'Fear not.'

abilities.name: Forewarned
abilities.text: When you arrive on a floor where they walk, you know it, unless they are hidden.

params.line: A clean light falls on the stair: a celestial creature walks this floor.

tiers.name: Lore
tiers.field_note: Exodus says Moses's face shone so after Sinai that the Israelites feared to come near, so he veiled it. In Greek myth, Semele saw Zeus in his full glory, and it killed her.

abilities.name: Shaded Eyes
abilities.text: You get +1 on saving throws against their blinding and confusion.
abilities.trigger_msg: Shaded Eyes: you look past the light, not into it.

tiers.name: Hunter
tiers.field_note: In Exodus, the Israelites daub lamb's blood on their doorposts, and when the destroyer comes for Egypt's firstborn, the Lord passes over every marked door.

abilities.name: Angel's Due
abilities.text: Their holy damage hurts you 5% less.
abilities.trigger_msg: Angel's Due: you bow your head, and the holy fire passes over.

tiers.name: Bane
tiers.field_note: Genesis tells how Abraham fed three strangers at Mamre who proved to be heavenly visitors, and Ovid how old Baucis and Philemon fed Jupiter and Mercury in disguise. Both hosts were richly rewarded.

abilities.name: Entertaining Angels
abilities.text: One lesser celestial in five arrives calm and leaves you be unless you strike first.
abilities.trigger_msg: Entertaining Angels: the light here lets you be.

grave_watch.name: The Grave Watch

boon.name: Vigil
boon.text: Necrotic and draining damage hurt you 5% less, from any source.

grave_watch.chronicle: I learned enough of every kind of the dead to keep watch over a grave all night.

wild_road.name: The Wild Road

boon.name: Ranger's Instinct
boon.text: You see one tile further in the dark.

wild_road.chronicle: I learned the wild things of the dark well enough to walk their roads like a ranger.

hellward_gate.name: The Hellward Gate

boon.name: Unbent Mind
boon.text: You get +1 on every saving throw against confusion, charm and fear, from anything.

hellward_gate.chronicle: I learned the tricks of everything that gets into a mind, and mine stopped bending.

heroes_road.name: The Hero's Road

boon.name: Hero's Nerve
boon.text: You get 1 more second on the maths clock against any boss.

heroes_road.chronicle: I learned the old stories well enough to walk the road the heroes walked.

loremaster.title: Loremaster
loremaster.chronicle: I came to know five families of monster down to the last weakness. Somebody should call me a loremaster.
